author: Pumpkin (shitpost arc)
text:
The most underrated thing in 2026 is keeping a personal notebook.

Not an AI notebook. Not a second brain with 20 apps connected together. Just one place where you write down things you learn.

I started doing this because I kept forgetting good ideas. A project would explain something interesting, I would think "I'll remember this," and two weeks later it was gone from my head.

Now I keep notes on projects, mistakes, posts that worked, and things I don't understand yet.

The surprising part is that the value isn't in writing the note.

It's in coming back to it months later.

You start seeing patterns.

You stop relearning the same lessons.

You make better connections because your old thoughts are still there waiting for you.

I think most people ignore this because taking notes doesn't look exciting. There is no hype around it and nobody can flex a notebook on CT.

But some of my best posts and ideas came from something I wrote down months earlier.

Even on 
@RallyOnChain
, I find myself going back to old notes before writing. Sometimes the difference between a generic post and an original one is simply remembering something everyone else forgot.

The internet rewards people who create.

A notebook quietly helps you become one of them.

What's one thing you wrote down months ago that still helps you today?
